groups.title: Division and remainder by zero in the primitive numeric lanes, at a transition-row write
groups.sharedSetting: One stateless-plus-stateful precept holding a decimal running total, an integer part count, and an event carrying a divisor argument; a single transition row writes `set PerPart = Total / Parts` (and the remainder variant) with the row's guard, the event's arg modifiers, and the field modifiers all available as premises. Every cell varies only which numeric lane the two operands sit in - integer/integer, integer/decimal, integer/number, decimal/decimal, number/number - times divide and modulo.
groups.authoringNotes: One cell per catalog site, so ten cells. The lane matters and must not be collapsed: the matrix's arg-bound interval-arithmetic validity argument (obligation-discharge-matrix-2026-07-19.md:206) explicitly covers the exact lanes only and names the `number` lane's IEEE rounding as an unstated open dependency, so the `number` cells inherit a weaker argument than the `integer`/`decimal` ones and must say so rather than reuse the exact-lane text. This is the group whose discharge story is already written in the matrix (Family 4, division with arg-constraint discharge), so it is the natural first file and the precedent the other division groups should match. Hazard: some evaluation-site categories in this group's region make premise class (d) (constraints holding in the pre-state) available, which means a discharge can run through a business `rule` used as a premise. Slice 2 verified at HEAD that such a discharge can be a false proof - `rule PlannedQuantity > 0` discharges a divide-by-zero via the CompositionalConstraint strategy while another handler sets the field to 0, and the whole file compiles clean (authored-expressiveness-gaps.md, Part 3, Defect B). So for any witness in this group whose discharge cites a `rule`, record builtStatus as unverified with that reason named, never as confirmed-by-clean-compile. Guard-based and modifier-based discharges in the same group are unaffected and may be recorded normally.
